newsitem.title: USA: US sells 1.1 mln bbl sour, 370,000 bbl sweet crude.
newsitem.headline: US sells 1.1 mln bbl sour, 370,000 bbl sweet crude.

text.p: The U.S. government Thursday sold 1.1 million barrels of sour crude and 370,000 barrels of sweet crude from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve in the first round of its latest auction, the Energy Department said.
Prices on the sour crude ranged from $21.80 to $22.25 per barrel, and prices for the sweet crude ranged from $23.70 to $24.40.
FINA Inc's Fina Oil and Chemical Co won 200,000 barrels of sour crude at $22.25 per barrel for pipeline delivery in November.
Coastal Corp's Coastal States Trading won 300,000 barrels of sour crude at $22.25 and another 300,000 barrels at $21.90 -- both batches for tanker delivery in November or December.
Mobil Corp was awarded 300,000 barrels of sour crude at $21.80 for pipeline delivery in October or November.
Basis Petroleum Inc, a subsidiary of Salomon Inc, took 195,000 barrels of sweet crude at $23.70 for pipeline delivery in November or December.
DuPont Co's Conoco Inc won 100,000 barrels of sweet crude at $24.40 for barge delivery in December.
Ashland Petroleum Co won 75,000 barrels of sweet crude at $23.87 for pipeline delivery in November.

The government offered up to 15 million barrels of light sour crude and 370,000 barrels of sweet crude in its new sale, which was ordered by Congress to raise $220 million to run the SPR in the 1997 fiscal year, which began October 1.
With the first round of sales, the government met 15 percent of its target.
Fresh bids for the ongoing auction are due November 4.
